concepts.title: A Half Point Ends the Argument
concepts.body: At -6.5, the favorite needs a seven-point win. At +6.5, the underdog can lose by six or win. The half point means neither side can tie.
concepts.takeaway: The .5 is there so the spread has a clear winner.
concepts.rationale: This makes the point spread feel like the game's second score: a simple rule that changes what a close finish means. The half point is the clean, shareable proof.
concepts.caption: A point spread turns a game into a margin question. At plus or minus 6.5, the half point removes the tie. That is the whole plot twist. #KnowTheOdds
concepts.alt: Intended Playbook RG sports-betting card titled 'A Half Point Ends the Argument.' It explains that a -6.5 favorite needs a seven-point win, while a +6.5 underdog can lose by six or win, beside a photo of friends discussing a close basketball game.

sources.note: Defines the favorite as needing to win by more than the spread and the underdog as able to lose by less or win outright. The source's -6.5/+6.5 examples establish the seven-point and six-point arithmetic; the half point eliminates ties.

concepts.title: The Slot Keeps No Tab
concepts.body: Every spin gets a new, independent result. Past losses do not load the next spin, and past wins do not make the next one less likely.
concepts.takeaway: The next spin starts fresh. The machine does not keep score.
concepts.rationale: The tab metaphor corrects the 'due' myth without scolding. It gives players one memorable way to understand independent outcomes.
concepts.caption: A slot does not keep a running tab of wins or losses. Each spin is a fresh result. The math is not holding a grudge. #KnowTheOdds
concepts.alt: Intended Playbook RG myth-check card titled 'The Slot Keeps No Tab.' It says every spin gets a new independent result and shows two friends talking beside an out-of-focus casino display.

concepts.title: The Total Is in the Tempo
concepts.body: $0.50 a spin, once every 3 seconds, is $10 a minute. Keep that pace for an hour and you have wagered $600—even on a penny machine.
concepts.takeaway: Check your pace: small bets can add up quickly.
concepts.rationale: This card puts the total in plain sight. Showing the minute-by-minute arithmetic turns a small per-spin amount into a pace players can recognize.
concepts.caption: At 20 spins a minute, a 50-cent spin is $10 a minute. Pace is part of the game math. #KnowTheOdds
concepts.alt: Intended Playbook RG card titled 'The Total Is in the Tempo.' It calculates that 50 cents per spin every three seconds equals $10 a minute and $600 wagered in an hour, with a photo of friends checking the time together.
